11	Agreed with the user on 2026-10-29/30 for the voice feature (built on [[voice-feature-branch-workflow]]):
12	- Calls: OpenAI GPT-Live (`gpt-live-1`, $0.05/min) with client delegation. GPT-Live talks; every real request goes to the existing `/api/chat` Moneo agent (user's chat model, GPT-6 Luna) in the same conversation. WebRTC set up server-side via `@ai-sdk/openai` live support, so the key never reaches the browser.
13	- While Moneo works, it says what it's doing out loud ("let me look through your transactions"), not only on screen.
14	- Several tasks at once: each request is its own parallel task, with **no limit**. Results are spoken as they arrive, held while the user is mid-sentence. Corrections (decided 2026-10-30): if the old task can still stop (only reading, no card made yet), stop it and start the new one. If it already made a card, let it finish, then run the corrected task, and auto-dismiss the old card with a "replaced" note. App code decides this, not the model. Each task also has an ✕ to stop it.
15	- Call personality: casual friend (short, warm, occasional "mm-hm"). Language: follow the user (English, German, mixed). Voice: Claude picks a natural default, plus a Settings voice picker with "Play sample".
16	- Confirm is tap-only on cards (tray during the call, and Overview "Waiting for you"). Voice never accepts.
17	- Mic: one button, same for tap or hold, with live words. At the end you choose **Send** (goes now; you can close the app) or **Done** (edit in the box). A voice note is just a spoken message, not a separate feature.
18	- Chat and artifact runs must keep going after the app is closed (Next `after()`, cancel only explicitly).
19	- After a call: summary card plus collapsible transcript in the chat. Both phone and desktop matter. No cost limits for now.
20	- Later items are in BACKLOG.md "Voice: later" (ElevenLabs, separate speech-to-text and text-to-speech pipeline, discreet mode, etc.).
21	
22	**Why:** the user wants the coolest real voice agent, but with financial truth staying in app code.
23	**How to apply:** build steps against these decisions; ask before changing any of them.

result.output:
--- 7e802aa7 Say call results one at a time, first finished first, and the next once Moneo has said it
Every finished result used to be handed to GPT-Live at once, so it blended them. What is still running is now read when a result goes out.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Entire-Checkpoint: 01M6694NXHX5D9Z3ZX9Q3MVYRW

--- 9490fbcd Have GPT-Live say results in full and answer progress and repeat questions itself
It no longer cuts a result to a sentence or two, and "what are you waiting for?" or "say that again" no longer starts a new request.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Entire-Checkpoint: 01M6694RJ711R8FZWMB3J7TF1K

--- 621665de Judge when Moneo has said a result by its voice, not its transcript
The transcript arrives ahead of the voice, so the next result was handed over while Moneo was still talking, and a user cutting in then cut off the wrong result. Moneo's voice is now metered every 100 ms: a result counts as said once Moneo has been quiet for 2.5 s, and the user talking before then means it was cut off. Progress updates no longer land mid-result, and dev builds log each hand-over and cut-off to the console.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Entire-Checkpoint: 01M66BSNDNH1CJX8791A59B2XQ

--- 901fdaef Have Moneo finish a result the user cut off, once it has answered them
Talking over a result stopped GPT-Live and the rest was lost. Now the cut result goes back first, after Moneo has answered the interruption, with a note to finish only what it hadn't said. A short mm-hm doesn't count.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Entire-Checkpoint: 01M66APE9P4MNNTS3PNG4R1TJM

--- 7b7a2528 Notice a cut-off result by when the user started talking, and wait out mid-sentence pauses
The user's words are transcribed after GPT-Live has already stopped, so judging by their arrival missed every interruption, and GPT-Live's mm-hm then marked the result as said. The audio-clock start of their words is compared with the end of Moneo's instead, and GPT-Live decides from its own transcript whether anything is left to say. Results also wait for a 1.5 s pause, not 0.7 s, so they don't land while the user says "uh… like…".
